findings.issue_text: `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` in `_ensure_processes_alive` (flusher.py:~248) is never true for spawn-context processes because `SpawnProcess` subclasses `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` directly and is a sibling of `multiprocessing.Process`, not a subclass — so `kill()` is dead code and hung flushers are never stopped; a hung process stays alive while a replacement polls the same shards, risking duplicate span payloads in Kafka and monitoring falsely reporting healthy via the shared `process_healthy_since` value (in thread mode the same duplicate-flusher outcome occurs since a replacement starts while the hung thread lives)

The new `--flusher-processes` CLI option has no visible plumbing to the `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` constructor (factory.py:41); if the runner's construction site passes a fixed kwarg set, `flusher_processes` is silently dropped, and the `None` default means 'one process per shard' (`max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`), silently spawning one flusher process per assigned shard instead of the documented default of 1 — N× Redis QPS and N× producers/connections per worker

With `flusher_processes > 1` in thread mode, multiple flusher threads concurrently invoke the same `produce_to_pipe` callable (flusher.py:~100-127); if the underlying implementation is a raw pipe/`Connection.send` write or a non-thread-safe producer, concurrent sends interleave and corrupt the byte stream between flusher and producing process, causing garbled or dropped Kafka payloads (silent span loss/corruption)

Metrics tag key inconsistency (flusher.py:~200): `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.flusher.segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, so dashboards/alerts slicing by `shard` silently miss every `wait_produce` series; additionally `flusher_unhealthy` emits individual shard ids under `shard` while timers emit comma-joined shard-groups under the same key, and the unhealthy counter fires once per shard in the group (count inflation)

The test's added `time.sleep(0.1)` in test_consumer.py:~61 is a no-op because the test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` for the entire process, so the promised synchronization doesn't exist and the flakiness (flusher thread happening to observe `current_drift = 9000` before `step.join()` sets the stopped flag) remains

`flusher_processes` is unvalidated (flusher.py:~48-56): `max_processes or len(assigned_shards)` turns `0` into 'one process per shard' (silently inverting operator intent), and negative values make `process_to_shards_map` an empty dict so the assignment loop crashes at startup with an opaque `KeyError: 0` unrelated to the actual bad input

New parameters inserted before `produce_to_pipe` in both `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` (factory.py:41) and `SpanFlusher.__init__` (flusher.py:47) break positional callers — a positional `produce_to_pipe` binds to `flusher_processes`/`max_processes`, causing `TypeError` at startup for `SpanFlusher` (`min(<callable>, len(shards))`) or silently using the truthy callable as the process cap for the factory

Dead `_create_process_for_shard` (flusher.py:~118-124) is referenced nowhere and, unlike `_ensure_processes_alive`, doesn't kill/replace the existing process — it overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` while the old process keeps running, so a future caller 'restarting a shard' would get two flushers on the same shards (duplicate segment production)

N+1 Redis I/O in the consume hot path: `submit` (flusher.py ~270) now calls `record_stored_segments` once per flusher process instead of one batched round trip over all shards, so per-message consumer latency scales linearly with `flusher_processes`
Parent holds one `SpansBuffer` (and its Redis client/pool) per process index, multiplying parent-side Redis connections
If `record_stored_segments` emits an untagged aggregate gauge, it is now emitted N times per submit with subset values, and statsd last-wins semantics cause underreporting

Crash-loop recovery cost multiplies by N and is paid synchronously in `submit` (flusher.py ~215-259): after a systemic fault kills all N processes, the next submit sequentially spawns up to N replacements inline, each re-importing the entire sentry codebase, blocking the consumer thread for N × spawn-time and stalling consumption and offset commits

`get_memory_info()` is fetched N times and summed as N duplicate copies (flusher.py ~283): each per-process buffer wraps the same Redis service so `used`/`available` are both scaled by N, N−1 fetches per message are pure waste, and the fragile sum-of-duplicates invariant means a future aggregation change (e.g., `max()`) would silently alter backpressure behavior
`--flusher-processes=0` falls through `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and silently means one process per shard — the opposite of disabling (flusher.py ~50-58)
A negative `flusher_processes` value makes `num_processes` negative: `range(-1)` yields an empty map and `i % -1 == 0` causes a `KeyError` at consumer startup (flusher.py ~50-58)

Factory-level default of `None` for `flusher_processes` means any non-CLI constructor now gets per-shard fan-out (a full interpreter + Kafka producer + Redis clients per shard) where the old behavior was always exactly 1 process

`join()` shares one deadline sequentially (flusher.py ~330-345): the first process can consume the entire join timeout leaving zero drain time for subsequent processes, and the `break` on deadline expiry skips `process.terminate()` for the current and all remaining processes, so segments already popped from Redis can be dropped mid-produce

Metric tag key mismatch (flusher.py ~188 vs ~200): `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` tag `shard` while `wait_produce` tags `shards`, splitting the same dimension across two keys so dashboards/alerts grouped by `shard` never see `wait_produce`

Comma-joined shard-set used as a metric tag value (flusher.py ~166, `shard_tag = ",".join(...)`): with fewer processes than shards (including the default of 1) the value is e.g. "0,1,2,…,31" — commas are tag separators in statsd/dogstatsd serialization, the value bloats every metric line, and every partition rebalance mints a new distinct value causing unbounded metric cardinality

Dead code `_create_process_for_shard` (flusher.py ~150-155) is never called since restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards`, its docstring falsely claims it is the restart path, and if wired up as written it would double-start a process for those shards because it never removes the old one from `self.processes`

The test's "give threads time" sleep is a no-op (tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py ~60-62): the test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a lambda, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` returns instantly, the described race is not actually addressed, and the test can remain flaky

Thread-mode "hang" restart leaves the hung thread running (flusher.py ~245-258): the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard skips the kill when `produce_to_pipe` is set, so a replacement thread starts while the hung one lives on, and both write the same shared `process_healthy_since`/`process_backpressure_since` Values, allowing a zombie thread waking up to mask a genuinely hung replacement

Removed attributes `self.buffer` and `self.process` may still be referenced in unchanged code (flusher.py): the unshown ~28-line gap between `submit`'s memory check and `close()` must contain `terminate()` (required by arroyo's `ProcessingStrategy` interface), and if `terminate` or any other unchanged method touches the deleted attributes, shutdown raises `AttributeError` on every deploy

In `join()` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:333-346), when the deadline is exhausted the `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the loop before `process.terminate()` runs for the current and all remaining flusher processes, leaving hung processes running indefinitely (still polling the same Redis shards and producing to Kafka alongside the replacement flusher, causing resource leaks, competing pollers, and double metrics); every remaining process should be terminated before/instead of breaking

In test_basic (tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:62), the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because `time.sleep` is monkeypatched to `lambda _: None` at the top of the test, so the drift-set → join()-sets-stopped race it claims to mitigate is unmitigated and the test remains racy; use an unpatched sleep/wait primitive or make the flusher deterministic

In `_ensure_processes_alive` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:~250), thread-mode restart never stops the old thread: `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()` leaves a hung thread running while a replacement thread for the same shards is started, so if the hung thread later unblocks, two threads poll the same shard set indefinitely (double fetch rate, double metrics, both writing the shared `Value`s)

In `__init__` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:50-62), there is no validation of `flusher_processes`: `max_processes or len(assigned_shards)` maps `--flusher-processes 0` to one process per shard (silently scaling up instead of down), and a negative value yields `num_processes < 0` → empty `process_to_shards_map` → `KeyError` at startup with no indication the CLI value is the cause; validate in the factory or clamp with `max(1, ...)`

Inconsistent metric tag keys for the shard dimension (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:~186, ~197, ~236): `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": <comma-joined list>}`, `wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": ...}`, and `flusher_unhealthy` uses `tags={"shard": <single int>}` — the same logical dimension under two keys and two value formats splits every dashboard/alert the health monitoring is supposed to feed, and comma-joined values may not round-trip cleanly through tag serialization

In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:41, `flusher_processes` is inserted before `produce_to_pipe` in the factory signature, so any existing caller passing `produce_to_pipe` positionally as the 6th argument now silently binds it to `flusher_processes` while `produce_to_pipe` falls back to `None`, flipping the flusher from pipe-mode threads to real subprocesses with a Kafka producer; appending the new parameter after `produce_to_pipe` would be safe

Health/restart checks only run inside `submit()` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:~264): if the consumer goes idle (no messages, or fetching paused after `MessageRejected`), `_ensure_processes_alive()` never runs, so a crashed or hung flusher process is neither detected nor restarted and its shards' segments sit unflushed in Redis until traffic resumes; the check belongs in `poll()` which runs more often (pre-existing, not worsened by this PR)

The race-fix time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic (tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:60-62) is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep to a lambda at its very first line; the intended synchronization never happens, join() sets stopped.value = True immediately after, and a flusher thread that just finished an iteration can exit without ever flushing at the new drift, leaving the PR's primary end-to-end test racy and prone to intermittent failure or passing while broken.

test_flusher_processes_limit (tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:82-120) verifies internal attributes rather than behavior: it never submits a message, never polls, asserts only on private internals (flusher.processes, flusher.max_processes, flusher.num_processes, fac._flusher), and its distribution check is vacuous since sum(len(shards)) == 4 passes even if all 4 shards are assigned to one process; nothing verifies that when shards share a process, spans from all shards are flushed and produced exactly once (a regression like a per-process SpansBuffer polling only its first assigned shard would pass this test).

The health-monitoring rework in src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py (~218-260) has zero test coverage: _ensure_processes_alive (per-process crash/hang detection, per-process restart counters, RuntimeError after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS, kill+respawn, per-shard flusher_unhealthy metrics) and the changed submit() aggregations (any-process backpressure raising MessageRejected, memory summed across per-shard buffers) are completely untested.

Behavioral asymmetry in flusher.py: in thread mode (produce_to_pipe), a hung thread is never killed before _create_process_for_shards respawns, leaving two flushers processing the same shards simultaneously.

The production multiprocessing (spawn) path in flusher.py (~90-125) is never exercised by any test: every test constructs the flusher with produce_to_pipe, which selects threading.Thread, so a pickling or constructor-signature regression in SpansBuffer(shards) would only surface in production at consumer startup.

A negative flusher_processes value crashes at startup with a KeyError: num_processes = min(-1, shards) yields an empty process_to_shards_map ({i: [] for i in range(-1)}), then self.process_to_shards_map[i % -1].append(shard) raises.

flusher_processes values of 0 and the constructor default None both silently mean one process per shard, diverging from the documented CLI default of 1 — an inconsistent-default footgun for any factory caller that doesn't pass the new kwarg.
No test verifies that the --flusher-processes click option is actually wired through to the factory.

Inconsistent metric tag keys in flusher.py (~191, 199, 203): spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes use tags={'shard': shard_tag} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses tags={'shards': shard_tag}, so any dashboard/alert keyed on one name won't see the other series.
The comma-joined multi-shard metric tag value is poor for grouping.
No test asserts the emitted metric tags.

join(timeout) with multiple processes (flusher.py ~326-345) skips terminating all remaining processes on deadline expiry: the break when remaining_time <= 0 exits the whole for loop before the terminate() for subsequent processes, so on a timeout, processes after the one being waited on are neither waited nor terminated; this changed shutdown behavior has no test for multi-process join/timeout.

In flusher.py (lines 186, 193-197, 200, 241-244), the metrics tag schema is inconsistent and the values are unsafe: the shard dimension is emitted three ways — produce/segment_size_bytes use tags={'shard': <comma-joined string>}, wait_produce uses tags={'shards': <comma-joined string>}, and flusher_unhealthy uses tags={'shard': <int>} per shard. Dashboards/alerts on spans.buffer.flusher.* fragment across two keys and two value formats, unhealthy shards cannot be correlated with their produce metrics, commas inside statsd-style tag values can split the tag string downstream, and segment_size_bytes goes from cardinality 1 to one tag value per distinct shard-assignment with rebalances minting new combinations forever — a cardinality time bomb on a per-segment hot metric.

flusher_processes is unvalidated (consumers/__init__.py:432-437, flusher.py:52, 61-64): `max_processes or len(assigned_shards)` maps 0 to one process per shard (a full spawned Python interpreter per shard — host OOM risk), and a negative value survives min() → range(negative) → zero processes and zero buffers. With zero buffers, submit()'s Redis-memory guard sums an empty list (available == 0 → never rejects) and the backpressure loop is empty, so the consumer silently keeps writing spans to Redis with nothing flushing until Redis OOMs; there is no click.IntRange(min=1) or clamp anywhere.

Two contradictory defaults exist for the same flusher_processes knob: the CLI default is 1 flusher process (consumers/__init__.py:434) while any direct construction of ProcessSpansStrategyFactory/SpanFlusher (factory.py:41, flusher.py:47, 52) defaults to None → one process per shard, so process topology silently depends on the entry path; the class docstring (flusher.py:29) falsely asserts 'Creates one process per shard' for the shipped default.

SpanFlusher accepts a SpansBuffer it no longer uses and builds a shadow buffer fleet (flusher.py:45, 52, 61-67, 91, 127-128, 270-271, 299-301): the constructor only reads buffer.assigned_shards, then constructs its own SpansBuffer(shards) per process group and routes parent-side operations (record_stored_segments, get_memory_info in submit) through the union of child buffers instead of the buffer it was handed. Buffer-construction knowledge now lives in two places (factory + flusher) and will drift, the buffer parameter is a misleading shard-list carrier, and parent-side stats fan out over N buffers for no functional gain.

In tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:12, 62, the 'give threads time' sleep is a monkeypatched no-op: test_basic patches time.sleep to a no-op and then calls time.sleep(0.1) commented 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change', so no time is actually yielded (the flusher thread's own sleeps are neutralized too, so it busy-spins). The race the change was meant to fix — the thread must flush before join() sets stopped — is still live and the test passes by GIL-scheduling luck; the comment also tells the next maintainer a falsehood. The real fix is to join the thread with a timeout or signal an event, not a sleep.

Dead method _create_process_for_shard (flusher.py:130-135) is a landmine: nothing in the PR calls it (restarts go through _create_process_for_shards directly), the near-identical name invites confusion, and if ever wired up it spawns a replacement process without killing the old one → two live flushers on the same shards → duplicate Kafka production. It should be deleted or made to kill-then-recreate.

join() (flusher.py:338-348) no longer terminates processes when the deadline is spent: next_step.join(timeout) can consume the whole timeout, and the process loop then hits remaining_time <= 0 and breaks before terminating anything, whereas the old code unconditionally terminated. Daemon=True caps the damage at interpreter exit, but any join-with-timeout path that returns early now leaves flushers running alongside a freshly started consumer.

Unreachable defensive branch `if not process: continue` (flusher.py:221-222): Process/Thread do not define __bool__/__len__ (always truthy) and self.processes is only ever assigned real objects, so the branch can never fire; it implies None can appear in the map and misleads readers about the lifecycle.

Comment at flusher.py:234 describes per-shard health checks that don't exist: 'Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy' sits above a process-level healthy_since comparison, and there is no per-shard health state. Readers auditing alerting behavior will be misled about what 'hang' means — it is per process-group, so one slow shard in a shared process indicts all its shards, which the metric loop then reports individually.

Six parallel dicts keyed by process_index (flusher.py:62-75, 127-128) — process_to_shards_map, processes, buffers, process_healthy_since, process_backpressure_since, process_restarts — must stay key-aligned through construction and every restart path (a restart already touches three of them, and the next editor must remember all six). A single dict[int, FlusherProcessState] dataclass would make desync impossible and shrink submit/_ensure_processes_alive.

Redundant `shards` argument to main (flusher.py:138-140) duplicates buffer.assigned_shards: the shard buffer already carries its shard list, and passing the list separately creates two sources of truth used for the sentry tag and metric tags — if they ever diverge, tags and health reporting lie.

Thread-mode 'restart' can't stop the old flusher (flusher.py:252-256): in produce_to_pipe (thread) mode, a 'hang' verdict spawns a replacement thread while the hung one keeps running (threads can't be killed; the isinstance guard skips kill), so two threads flush the same shards until MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS raises. Bounded, but the health-restart contract silently doesn't hold in thread mode.

terminate() may still reference the deleted self.process/self.buffer in flusher.py: Arroyo's ProcessingStrategy requires terminate(), no hunk in the PR shows it, yet every shown method was migrated off self.process/self.buffer. If the existing terminate() calls self.process.terminate()/.kill() or reads self.buffer, every consumer shutdown now raises AttributeError — and the tests never call terminate(), so CI won't catch it.

current_drift is one shared Value across all flusher processes (flusher.py:57, 118): stopped is legitimately global, but current_drift was the single flusher's private clock adjustment and is now shared by N processes. If the unshown part of main() writes drift from its own shards' progress, processes clobber each other and a lagging process can compute a too-advanced 'now' (skipped segments) or everyone re-flushes (duplicates); the write path isn't visible in the diff and needs verification.

SpanFlusher.join() timeout path: when the deadline expires, the break exits the loop before calling process.terminate(), so processes not yet iterated are never terminated — during rebalance this leaves rogue daemon flusher processes polling Redis shards that may have been reassigned to another consumer (racing the new owner for segments, risking duplicate or stolen production) each with a live Kafka producer, breaking the original unconditional terminate() contract

SpanFlusher.join() gives self.next_step.join(timeout) the full timeout up front instead of the remaining time, so if next_step consumes it, remaining_time <= 0 is true on the first iteration and zero processes are terminated

In test_basic, monkeypatch.setattr('time.sleep', lambda _: None) globally replaces time.sleep with a no-op, so the newly added time.sleep(0.1) meant to fix the race (a flusher thread that hasn't polled after current_drift.value = 9000 exits when step.join() sets stopped.value = True, making (msg,) = messages fail on an empty list) provides no synchronization and the flake persists; the fix should wait on an actual condition (poll until messages is non-empty with a bounded deadline, or use an Event)

flusher.py __init__: self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) treats --flusher-processes 0 as falsy, silently inverting it to one process per shard (maximum parallelism), the opposite of operator intent, spawning far more processes/Redis connections/Kafka producers than intended

flusher.py __init__: a negative --flusher-processes value (no click range validation, type=int only) yields num_processes = min(-1, N) = -1 and an empty process_to_shards_map from {i: [] for i in range(-1)}, then i % -1 == 0 for all i makes self.process_to_shards_map[0].append(shard) raise an opaque KeyError: 0 at startup with no hint that --flusher-processes was the cause

_ensure_processes_alive: process.kill() is guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), so in thread mode (produce_to_pipe set) a hang restart starts a new thread for the same shards while the old hung thread keeps running — if the old thread recovers, both poll the same shards and call produce_to_pipe, causing duplicate segment production; this replaces the old loud Thread.kill() AttributeError with a new silent failure mode

shard_tag is a comma-joined list of all shards in the process (e.g. '0,1,2,...,63'), so timer tag cardinality scales with the number of distinct shard-subsets across consumers rather than with shard count; the timers should match the sane per-shard form used by the flusher_unhealthy counter

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` in `_ensure_processes_alive` (flusher.py:~248) is never true for spawn-context processes because `SpawnProcess` subclasses `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` directly and is a sibling of `multiprocessing.Process`, not a subclass — so `kill()` is dead code and hung flushers are never stopped; a hung process stays alive while a replacement polls the same shards, risking duplicate span payloads in Kafka and monitoring falsely reporting healthy via the shared `process_healthy_since` value (in thread mode the same duplicate-flusher outcome occurs since a replacement starts while the hung thread lives)

adjudication_records.issue_text: With `flusher_processes > 1` in thread mode, multiple flusher threads concurrently invoke the same `produce_to_pipe` callable (flusher.py:~100-127); if the underlying implementation is a raw pipe/`Connection.send` write or a non-thread-safe producer, concurrent sends interleave and corrupt the byte stream between flusher and producing process, causing garbled or dropped Kafka payloads (silent span loss/corruption)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `SpanFlusher` from a single background worker to potentially multiple workers (`self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`) and, when `produce_to_pipe` is provided, it uses `threading.Thread` (see `_create_process_for_shards`: `make_process = threading.Thread` and `target = partial(SpanFlusher.main, shard_buffer)`). All created threads receive the same `produce_to_pipe` callable and can call it concurrently inside `main()` via `produce(kafka_payload)`. There is no locking/serialization around `produce_to_pipe`, so the finding correctly identifies a new concurrency requirement: `produce_to_pipe` must be thread-safe. However, the diff does not show that `produce_to_pipe` is a raw pipe/`Connection.send` or otherwise non-thread-safe in this PR, so actual byte-stream corruption/data loss cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 Redis I/O in the consume hot path: `submit` (flusher.py ~270) now calls `record_stored_segments` once per flusher process instead of one batched round trip over all shards, so per-message consumer latency scales linearly with `flusher_processes`

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the diff changes `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` to a loop over `self.buffers.values()` calling `record_stored_segments()` once per per-process/shard-buffer (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()`). Since `submit` is described in-code as not a hot path but still called per message, this change does make the per-message work scale with the number of flusher processes/buffers. The finding’s specific claim that this is N+1 Redis I/O can’t be proven from the diff alone (we can’t see whether `record_stored_segments()` performs Redis round trips), but the scaling/perf regression risk introduced by the loop is diff-grounded and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Parent holds one `SpansBuffer` (and its Redis client/pool) per process index, multiplying parent-side Redis connections

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__` / `_create_process_for_shards`, the parent now constructs a separate `SpansBuffer(shards)` per `process_index` and stores them in `self.buffers` (`self.buffers[process_index] = shard_buffer`). The parent then actively uses all these buffers in `submit()` (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` and `buffer.get_memory_info()`), so it is indeed holding N `SpansBuffer` instances concurrently. If `SpansBuffer` encapsulates a Redis client/pool (not shown in this diff), this design would multiply parent-side Redis connections/resources. This is a concrete resource/architecture concern introduced by the change, but not a directly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: If `record_stored_segments` emits an untagged aggregate gauge, it is now emitted N times per submit with subset values, and statsd last-wins semantics cause underreporting

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `SpanFlusher.submit` from a single `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` call to calling `record_stored_segments()` once per per-process shard buffer (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()`). adjudication_records.issue_text: Crash-loop recovery cost multiplies by N and is paid synchronously in `submit` (flusher.py ~215-259): after a systemic fault kills all N processes, the next submit sequentially spawns up to N replacements inline, each re-importing the entire sentry codebase, blocking the consumer thread for N × spawn-time and stalling consumption and offset commits

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes SpanFlusher from a single background process/thread to multiple processes (one per shard group) and calls `_ensure_processes_alive()` synchronously from `submit()` (see `submit` now calling `_ensure_processes_alive` and `_ensure_processes_alive` looping over `self.processes`). On detecting an unhealthy/dead process, it kills it and immediately restarts it inline via `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, which constructs a new `SpansBuffer` and starts a new `multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process` when `produce_to_pipe is None`. If a systemic fault kills all N flusher processes, the next `submit()` will indeed iterate and sequentially spawn up to N replacements on the consumer thread, incurring roughly N× process spawn/import cost and stalling consumption/commits. This is a concrete performance/availability concern introduced by the new multi-process restart logic, but not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `get_memory_info()` is fetched N times and summed as N duplicate copies (flusher.py ~283): each per-process buffer wraps the same Redis service so `used`/`available` are both scaled by N, N−1 fetches per message are pure waste, and the fragile sum-of-duplicates invariant means a future aggregation change (e.g., `max()`) would silently alter backpressure behavior

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the diff changes memory accounting from a single `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` call to iterating all per-process buffers: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`, then summing `used` and `available` (flusher.py ~296). This definitely increases the number of `get_memory_info()` calls to N (number of flusher shard-buffers). Whether those calls are duplicates depends on `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` internals (not shown), so the claim about scaling `used/available` by N and fragility of the sum cannot be fully verified from the diff, but the extra per-message work introduced by the change is real and could be wasteful if each buffer queries the same underlying service.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `--flusher-processes=0` falls through `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and silently means one process per shard — the opposite of disabling (flusher.py ~50-58)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `max_processes=0` as falsy and replaces it with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. The new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is `type=int` with no lower-bound validation, so `0` is an accepted value and will unexpectedly result in `num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...)) == len(...)` (i.e., one process per shard) rather than 0 or an error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A negative `flusher_processes` value makes `num_processes` negative: `range(-1)` yields an empty map and `i % -1 == 0` causes a `KeyError` at consumer startup (flusher.py ~50-58)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will keep a negative `max_processes` (it’s truthy). Then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` can become negative. That makes `process_to_shards_map = {i: [] for i in range(self.num_processes)}` empty (`range(-1)`), but the subsequent loop does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and then indexes `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index]`, which will raise `KeyError` at startup. The new CLI option `--flusher-processes` accepts arbitrary ints and no validation is shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Factory-level default of `None` for `flusher_processes` means any non-CLI constructor now gets per-shard fan-out (a full interpreter + Kafka producer + Redis clients per shard) where the old behavior was always exactly 1 process

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the default flusher parallelism from a single background worker to per-shard fan-out when no limit is provided. `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` adds `flusher_processes: int | None = None` and passes it through as `max_processes=self.flusher_processes`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, which yields `len(assigned_shards)` when `max_processes` is `None`—i.e., one process/thread per shard. Previously `_create_process()` created exactly one process/thread regardless of shard count. This is a significant default behavior/resource-footprint change; not necessarily a functional correctness bug, but an important review concern grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `join()` shares one deadline sequentially (flusher.py ~330-345): the first process can consume the entire join timeout leaving zero drain time for subsequent processes, and the `break` on deadline expiry skips `process.terminate()` for the current and all remaining processes, so segments already popped from Redis can be dropped mid-produce

adjudication_records.issue_text: Comma-joined shard-set used as a metric tag value (flusher.py ~166, `shard_tag = ",".join(...)`): with fewer processes than shards (including the default of 1) the value is e.g. "0,1,2,…,31" — commas are tag separators in statsd/dogstatsd serialization, the value bloats every metric line, and every partition rebalance mints a new distinct value causing unbounded metric cardinality

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main` the diff adds `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` and uses it as a metric tag value (e.g. `metrics.timer(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timer(..., tags={"shards": shard_tag})`). If the statsd/dogstatsd tag serialization uses commas to separate tags, embedding commas in a tag value can break tag parsing and/or inflate each metric line. Also, because `shard_tag` encodes the full shard set handled by a process, rebalances can produce many distinct tag values, increasing metric cardinality. This is a concrete, diff-grounded operational/observability concern rather than a core functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Thread-mode "hang" restart leaves the hung thread running (flusher.py ~245-258): the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard skips the kill when `produce_to_pipe` is set, so a replacement thread starts while the hung one lives on, and both write the same shared `process_healthy_since`/`process_backpressure_since` Values, allowing a zombie thread waking up to mask a genuinely hung replacement

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (`produce_to_pipe` set), `_create_process_for_shards` creates a `threading.Thread` (not a `multiprocessing.Process`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, when a thread is deemed unhealthy (`hang` via `process_healthy_since[...]` age) or dead, the restart path only attempts `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so threads are never stopped before starting a replacement (`self._create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). The old thread still holds references to the same `mp_context.Value` objects passed in (`process_healthy_since[...]` / `process_backpressure_since[...]`) and can continue updating them if it resumes, masking issues and potentially duplicating work (both threads flushing the same shard set). This problematic behavior is directly implied by the diff’s restart logic and shared Value usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In `_ensure_processes_alive` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:~250), thread-mode restart never stops the old thread: `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()` leaves a hung thread running while a replacement thread for the same shards is started, so if the hung thread later unblocks, two threads poll the same shard set indefinitely (double fetch rate, double metrics, both writing the shared `Value`s)

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` when `produce_to_pipe` is set, and `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts an unhealthy worker by starting a new thread/process via `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: In `__init__` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:50-62), there is no validation of `flusher_processes`: `max_processes or len(assigned_shards)` maps `--flusher-processes 0` to one process per shard (silently scaling up instead of down), and a negative value yields `num_processes < 0` → empty `process_to_shards_map` → `KeyError` at startup with no indication the CLI value is the cause; validate in the factory or clamp with `max(1, ...)`

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag keys for the shard dimension (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:~186, ~197, ~236): `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": <comma-joined list>}`, `wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": ...}`, and `flusher_unhealthy` uses `tags={"shard": <single int>}` — the same logical dimension under two keys and two value formats splits every dashboard/alert the health monitoring is supposed to feed, and comma-joined values may not round-trip cleanly through tag serialization

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys and value formats for the same shard dimension in `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use key `shard` with a comma-joined string of multiple shard ids, while `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses key `shards`, and `_ensure_processes_alive` reports `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` with `tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard}` where `shard` is a single int. This will split/fragment metrics series and makes shard-based dashboards/alerts inconsistent, and the comma-joined multi-shard value is a different cardinality/format than the single-shard tags.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:41, `flusher_processes` is inserted before `produce_to_pipe` in the factory signature, so any existing caller passing `produce_to_pipe` positionally as the 6th argument now silently binds it to `flusher_processes` while `produce_to_pipe` falls back to `None`, flipping the flusher from pipe-mode threads to real subprocesses with a Kafka producer; appending the new parameter after `produce_to_pipe` would be safe

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` adding `flusher_processes: int | None = None` *before* `produce_to_pipe` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py). That is a real API-compatibility hazard: any external/other call site using positional arguments for the old last parameter would now bind that value to `flusher_processes` and leave `produce_to_pipe` as `None`, changing behavior (thread mode vs process mode). However, this diff does not show any existing positional callers actually being broken (new/updated tests use keyword args), so the concrete breakage claimed cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Health/restart checks only run inside `submit()` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:~264): if the consumer goes idle (no messages, or fetching paused after `MessageRejected`), `_ensure_processes_alive()` never runs, so a crashed or hung flusher process is neither detected nor restarted and its shards' segments sit unflushed in Redis until traffic resumes; the check belongs in `poll()` which runs more often (pre-existing, not worsened by this PR)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher`, health/restart monitoring is only invoked from `submit()` via `_ensure_processes_alive()` (see call at `submit`: `self._ensure_processes_alive()`). The `poll()` implementation in the diff only delegates to `self.next_step.poll()` and does not perform any liveness/health checks. Therefore, if no messages are submitted (idle consumer, or fetching halted upstream after `MessageRejected`), a crashed/hung flusher process would not be detected/restarted by this code path, matching the finding’s concern about segments remaining unflushed until traffic resumes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The race-fix time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic (tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:60-62) is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep to a lambda at its very first line; the intended synchronization never happens, join() sets stopped.value = True immediately after, and a flusher thread that just finished an iteration can exit without ever flushing at the new drift, leaving the PR's primary end-to-end test racy and prone to intermittent failure or passing while broken.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the first line still does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, patching the global `time.sleep`. The newly added synchronization `time.sleep(0.1)` (after the extra `step.poll()`) therefore becomes a no-op, so it cannot provide the intended wait for the flusher thread(s) to process after `current_drift` is changed. Immediately after, `step.join()` sets `self.stopped.value = True` in `SpanFlusher.join()`, which can cause the background thread(s) to exit their loop without doing additional work, leaving the test potentially racy/flaky and undermining the intended race fix.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_flusher_processes_limit (tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:82-120) verifies internal attributes rather than behavior: it never submits a message, never polls, asserts only on private internals (flusher.processes, flusher.max_processes, flusher.num_processes, fac._flusher), and its distribution check is vacuous since sum(len(shards)) == 4 passes even if all 4 shards are assigned to one process; nothing verifies that when shards share a process, spans from all shards are flushed and produced exactly once (a regression like a per-process SpansBuffer polling only its first assigned shard would pass this test).

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the assertions are entirely about private/internal state (`fac._flusher`, `len(flusher.processes)`, `flusher.max_processes`, `flusher.num_processes`, and `process_to_shards_map`) and the test never drives the flusher via `submit()` (no messages) or even `poll()` to exercise flushing/producing. The “distribution” assertion only checks `sum(len(shards) ...) == 4`, which does not validate per-process coverage or that shard-sharing works correctly end-to-end (e.g., a regression where a per-process `SpansBuffer` only polls a subset of its assigned shards could still satisfy these internal-count checks). This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in testing of the newly added shard-to-process multiplexing logic, not a proven runtime defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The health-monitoring rework in src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py (~218-260) has zero test coverage: _ensure_processes_alive (per-process crash/hang detection, per-process restart counters, RuntimeError after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS, kill+respawn, per-shard flusher_unhealthy metrics) and the changed submit() aggregations (any-process backpressure raising MessageRejected, memory summed across per-shard buffers) are completely untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new per-process health/restart logic in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive()` (looping over `self.processes`, per-process `process_healthy_since`/`process_backpressure_since`, per-process restart counters, `kill()` + `_create_process_for_shards()`, and per-shard `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` metrics), plus `submit()` now aggregates `record_stored_segments()`, backpressure rejection across *any* process, and sums memory info across `self.buffers`. The new/updated tests only assert process count/shard distribution (`test_flusher_processes_limit`) and adjust an assertion to `any(x.value ...)` (`test_flusher.py`), but they do not exercise crash/hang detection, restart exhaustion (`MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` -> `RuntimeError`), kill/respawn behavior, metric tagging per shard/cause, MessageRejected from per-process backpressure, or the memory aggregation behavior. So the finding is a concrete missing-coverage concern grounded in the diff rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral asymmetry in flusher.py: in thread mode (produce_to_pipe), a hung thread is never killed before _create_process_for_shards respawns, leaving two flushers processing the same shards simultaneously.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a worker is deemed unhealthy due to a hang (`time.time() - self.process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`), the restart path only attempts `process.kill()` if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. In thread mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), the worker is a `threading.Thread`, so it is not killed/stopped, yet `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` is still called, spawning a new thread for the same `shards`. Since `self.stopped` is not set during restart (only in `join()`), the old hung thread can remain alive and potentially resume, leading to two flushers concurrently processing the same shards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The production multiprocessing (spawn) path in flusher.py (~90-125) is never exercised by any test: every test constructs the flusher with produce_to_pipe, which selects threading.Thread, so a pickling or constructor-signature regression in SpansBuffer(shards) would only surface in production at consumer startup.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows SpanFlusher chooses multiprocessing spawn only when produce_to_pipe is None (flusher.py: in _create_process_for_shards, make_process = mp_context.Process vs threading.Thread). The updated/added tests construct ProcessSpansStrategyFactory with produce_to_pipe=messages.append (test_consumer.py test_basic and new test_flusher_processes_limit) and existing flusher test uses a callback too, so they exercise only the threading path. That means regressions in the production spawn/pickling path (e.g., passing the new SpansBuffer(shards) into a spawned process and the updated main() signature taking shards) wouldn’t be caught by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A negative flusher_processes value crashes at startup with a KeyError: num_processes = min(-1, shards) yields an empty process_to_shards_map ({i: [] for i in range(-1)}), then self.process_to_shards_map[i % -1].append(shard) raises.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will keep a negative value (e.g. `-1`) because it is truthy. Then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becomes negative, making `process_to_shards_map` empty (`{i: [] for i in range(self.num_processes)}` with `range(-1)`), but the subsequent loop still does `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`, which will raise `KeyError` (since the dict has no keys). The new click option `--flusher-processes` has no validation to prevent negative values, so this crash is reachable at startup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher_processes values of 0 and the constructor default None both silently mean one process per shard, diverging from the documented CLI default of 1 — an inconsistent-default footgun for any factory caller that doesn't pass the new kwarg.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats both `None` and `0` as falsy and thus as “no limit”, resulting in `num_processes = len(assigned_shards)` (one process per shard). This conflicts with the new CLI option default of `1` (`click.Option(..., default=1, help="... Defaults to 1.")`) and creates a footgun: callers of `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` that omit `flusher_processes` (default `None`) or pass `0` will unexpectedly get per-shard processes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test verifies that the --flusher-processes click option is actually wired through to the factory.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new Click option `--flusher-processes` in `src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py`, and the factory now accepts `flusher_processes` and forwards it to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)` (`factory.py`). However, the added test (`test_flusher_processes_limit`) only instantiates `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(..., flusher_processes=2, ...)` directly; it does not exercise the Click option parsing or the wiring from CLI/config into the factory arguments. Nothing else in the diff adds such a wiring test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag keys in flusher.py (~191, 199, 203): spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes use tags={'shard': shard_tag} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses tags={'shards': shard_tag}, so any dashboard/alert keyed on one name won't see the other series.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main` the diff introduces metric tags using two different keys for the same shard identifier: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`. This inconsistency is directly visible in the diff and can fragment metric series/dashboards, but it does not break functional behavior of the flusher itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The comma-joined multi-shard metric tag value is poor for grouping.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main` the diff introduces `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` and uses it as a metrics tag value (e.g. `metrics.timer(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, `metrics.timing(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`). When one process handles multiple shards, this produces composite tag values like `"0,2"`, which will fragment/impair grouping by shard and can increase tag cardinality compared to tagging by a single shard or by `process_index`/`num_shards`. This is an observability/metrics design issue, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test asserts the emitted metric tags.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds/changes metric emissions to include specific tags (e.g. `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, `metrics.timing(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, and `metrics.timer(..., tags={"shards": shard_tag})` in `SpanFlusher.main`), and also adds per-shard tags to `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy`. The updated/added tests (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`, and the assertion change in `test_flusher.py`) do not assert that these metric tags are present or correct; they only check behavior like message production and backpressure flags. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for newly introduced tagged-metrics behavior, but not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join(timeout) with multiple processes (flusher.py ~326-345) skips terminating all remaining processes on deadline expiry: the break when remaining_time <= 0 exits the whole for loop before the terminate() for subsequent processes, so on a timeout, processes after the one being waited on are neither waited nor terminated; this changed shutdown behavior has no test for multi-process join/timeout.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the loop over self.processes breaks entirely when remaining_time <= 0 (deadline exceeded) before reaching later processes. Because the terminate() call is inside the per-process loop, any processes after the break are neither waited on nor terminated. This is a behavioral regression from the prior single-process logic which always called terminate() after the wait loop, and there’s no test covering multi-process join(timeout) shutdown semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In flusher.py (lines 186, 193-197, 200, 241-244), the metrics tag schema is inconsistent and the values are unsafe: the shard dimension is emitted three ways — produce/segment_size_bytes use tags={'shard': <comma-joined string>}, wait_produce uses tags={'shards': <comma-joined string>}, and flusher_unhealthy uses tags={'shard': <int>} per shard. Dashboards/alerts on spans.buffer.flusher.* fragment across two keys and two value formats, unhealthy shards cannot be correlated with their produce metrics, commas inside statsd-style tag values can split the tag string downstream, and segment_size_bytes goes from cardinality 1 to one tag value per distinct shard-assignment with rebalances minting new combinations forever — a cardinality time bomb on a per-segment hot metric.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys and value formats in `SpanFlusher.main` and `_ensure_processes_alive`: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use key `shard` with a comma-joined string (`shard_tag`), while `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses key `shards`, and `_ensure_processes_alive` emits `metrics.incr(..., tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})` with `shard` as an int per shard. This will fragment dashboards/alerts across different tag schemas and makes correlating unhealthy-per-shard with produce metrics harder; it also introduces potentially high-cardinality tag values by using combinations of shards as a tag value. While not a functional correctness bug, it is a concrete monitoring/metrics-quality issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher_processes is unvalidated (consumers/__init__.py:432-437, flusher.py:52, 61-64): `max_processes or len(assigned_shards)` maps 0 to one process per shard (a full spawned Python interpreter per shard — host OOM risk), and a negative value survives min() → range(negative) → zero processes and zero buffers. With zero buffers, submit()'s Redis-memory guard sums an empty list (available == 0 → never rejects) and the backpressure loop is empty, so the consumer silently keeps writing spans to Redis with nothing flushing until Redis OOMs; there is no click.IntRange(min=1) or clamp anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new CLI option `--flusher-processes` with `type=int` and no range/validation, and passes it through to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` makes `0` mean “one process per shard” (potentially spawning many Python processes), and a negative value is truthy so it survives into `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))`, which can become negative. That yields an empty `process_to_shards_map` and will likely error during shard assignment (`self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`), i.e., misconfiguration can cause bad behavior/crash. The finding’s later claim about ‘silently keeps writing with zero buffers’ isn’t supported because the negative case would fail earlier, but the core issue (no validation/clamp; 0 and negative are problematic) is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Two contradictory defaults exist for the same flusher_processes knob: the CLI default is 1 flusher process (consumers/__init__.py:434) while any direct construction of ProcessSpansStrategyFactory/SpanFlusher (factory.py:41, flusher.py:47, 52) defaults to None → one process per shard, so process topology silently depends on the entry path; the class docstring (flusher.py:29) falsely asserts 'Creates one process per shard' for the shipped default.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the CLI adds `--flusher-processes` with `default=1` (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py), while `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` defaults `flusher_processes` to `None` and passes it through to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)` (factory.py). In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so `None` implies one process per shard, but the CLI entry path implies a single process by default. This makes the default process topology differ depending on construction path, and the docstring claim 'Creates one process per shard' is not generally true when `max_processes` is set (e.g., CLI default 1). This is a concrete inconsistency/documentation issue, but not necessarily a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SpanFlusher accepts a SpansBuffer it no longer uses and builds a shadow buffer fleet (flusher.py:45, 52, 61-67, 91, 127-128, 270-271, 299-301): the constructor only reads buffer.assigned_shards, then constructs its own SpansBuffer(shards) per process group and routes parent-side operations (record_stored_segments, get_memory_info in submit) through the union of child buffers instead of the buffer it was handed. Buffer-construction knowledge now lives in two places (factory + flusher) and will drift, the buffer parameter is a misleading shard-list carrier, and parent-side stats fan out over N buffers for no functional gain.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows SpanFlusher.__init__ no longer retains/uses the passed `buffer` beyond reading `buffer.assigned_shards` to derive `max_processes` and shard-to-process mapping, then constructs new `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances per process (`shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` in `_create_process_for_shards`). Parent-side operations in `submit` fan out across `self.buffers.values()` (`record_stored_segments()` and `get_memory_info()`), not the original buffer. This makes the `buffer` parameter effectively a shard-list carrier and duplicates buffer-construction responsibility between caller and flusher; it’s a concrete, diff-grounded design/maintenance concern, but not a demonstrable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:12, 62, the 'give threads time' sleep is a monkeypatched no-op: test_basic patches time.sleep to a no-op and then calls time.sleep(0.1) commented 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change', so no time is actually yielded (the flusher thread's own sleeps are neutralized too, so it busy-spins). The race the change was meant to fix — the thread must flush before join() sets stopped — is still live and the test passes by GIL-scheduling luck; the comment also tells the next maintainer a falsehood. The real fix is to join the thread with a timeout or signal an event, not a sleep.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `test_basic` does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` and later calls `time.sleep(0.1)` with a comment about giving threads time (tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py). That sleep will be a no-op under the monkeypatch, so the comment is misleading and it does not actually yield time as intended. The further claim that this definitively leaves a specific race “still live” is plausible but not strictly provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead method _create_process_for_shard (flusher.py:130-135) is a landmine: nothing in the PR calls it (restarts go through _create_process_for_shards directly), the near-identical name invites confusion, and if ever wired up it spawns a replacement process without killing the old one → two live flushers on the same shards → duplicate Kafka production. It should be deleted or made to kill-then-recreate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` which is not referenced anywhere in the shown changes (restarts happen in `_ensure_processes_alive` via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). As implemented, `_create_process_for_shard` would call `_create_process_for_shards` without killing/terminating an existing process for that shard group, and `_create_process_for_shards` always starts a new process/thread and overwrites `self.processes[process_index]`, which could leave the old one running. That is a maintainability/footgun risk, but it is not a currently triggered, verifiable defect in this diff since the method is unused.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() (flusher.py:338-348) no longer terminates processes when the deadline is spent: next_step.join(timeout) can consume the whole timeout, and the process loop then hits remaining_time <= 0 and breaks before terminating anything, whereas the old code unconditionally terminated. Daemon=True caps the damage at interpreter exit, but any join-with-timeout path that returns early now leaves flushers running alongside a freshly started consumer.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), after computing `deadline` and calling `self.next_step.join(timeout)`, the new loop checks `remaining_time = deadline - time.time()` and `break`s if `remaining_time <= 0` before reaching the per-process `terminate()` call. If `next_step.join(timeout)` consumes the full timeout (or the deadline is exceeded between processes), the function can exit without terminating any/all flusher processes, whereas the old code always called `self.process.terminate()` unconditionally after the wait loop. This can leave daemonized flusher processes running after join-with-timeout returns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unreachable defensive branch `if not process: continue` (flusher.py:221-222): Process/Thread do not define __bool__/__len__ (always truthy) and self.processes is only ever assigned real objects, so the branch can never fire; it implies None can appear in the map and misleads readers about the lifecycle.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, the loop does `for process_index, process in self.processes.items(): if not process: continue`. In this diff, `self.processes` is only populated in `_create_process_for_shards` with a freshly created `Process`/`Thread` object (`self.processes[process_index] = process`) and there is no code path shown that assigns `None`/falsy sentinels into the dict. `multiprocessing.Process` / `threading.Thread` instances are truthy by default, so this defensive branch is effectively unreachable and may mislead readers into thinking `None` is a valid lifecycle state in the map. This is a maintainability/clarity issue, not a demonstrated correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Comment at flusher.py:234 describes per-shard health checks that don't exist: 'Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy' sits above a process-level healthy_since comparison, and there is no per-shard health state. Readers auditing alerting behavior will be misled about what 'hang' means — it is per process-group, so one slow shard in a shared process indicts all its shards, which the metric loop then reports individually.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, the comment above the hang check says “Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy”, but the code only compares `time.time()` against `self.process_healthy_since[process_index].value`, which is a single per-process/group timestamp (updated in `main()` via `healthy_since.value = system_now`). There is no per-shard health state, so the comment is misleading about what “hang” means, especially since the subsequent metrics loop reports the same cause for each shard in that process group.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Six parallel dicts keyed by process_index (flusher.py:62-75, 127-128) — process_to_shards_map, processes, buffers, process_healthy_since, process_backpressure_since, process_restarts — must stay key-aligned through construction and every restart path (a restart already touches three of them, and the next editor must remember all six). A single dict[int, FlusherProcessState] dataclass would make desync impossible and shrink submit/_ensure_processes_alive.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `SpanFlusher.__init__` introduces multiple parallel dicts keyed by `process_index` (`process_to_shards_map`, `processes`, `buffers`, `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`, `process_restarts`). Construction initializes most of them via `range(self.num_processes)`, while `processes`/`buffers` are populated later in `_create_process_for_shards`. Restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` which updates only some structures (e.g., `processes`, `buffers`, and `process_healthy_since[process_index]`), relying on the others to already exist and remain consistent. This is a real maintainability/robustness concern grounded in the diff (risk of future edits forgetting to update all per-process state), but it is not a presently verifiable functional defect in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redundant `shards` argument to main (flusher.py:138-140) duplicates buffer.assigned_shards: the shard buffer already carries its shard list, and passing the list separately creates two sources of truth used for the sentry tag and metric tags — if they ever diverge, tags and health reporting lie.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, a `SpansBuffer(shards)` is constructed and then `shards` is also passed separately into `SpanFlusher.main(buffer, shards, ...)`. Inside `main`, `shards` is used for the Sentry tag (`sentry_spans_buffer_shards`) and for metric tags, while the actual work uses `buffer` (which presumably already encodes the shard assignment). The diff does not show an actual divergence/defect (both values originate from the same `shards` list at construction time), but it does introduce redundant parallel state that could drift in future refactors and lead to misleading tagging/observability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Thread-mode 'restart' can't stop the old flusher (flusher.py:252-256): in produce_to_pipe (thread) mode, a 'hang' verdict spawns a replacement thread while the hung one keeps running (threads can't be killed; the isinstance guard skips kill), so two threads flush the same shards until MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS raises. Bounded, but the health-restart contract silently doesn't hold in thread mode.

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` (see `make_process = threading.Thread`). On an unhealthy/hang condition, `_ensure_processes_alive` will restart via `self._create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` but only attempts to kill the old worker if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`; threads are not stopped (`process.kill()` is skipped and no other stop signal is set). adjudication_records.issue_text: SpanFlusher.join() timeout path: when the deadline expires, the break exits the loop before calling process.terminate(), so processes not yet iterated are never terminated — during rebalance this leaves rogue daemon flusher processes polling Redis shards that may have been reassigned to another consumer (racing the new owner for segments, risking duplicate or stolen production) each with a live Kafka producer, breaking the original unconditional terminate() contract

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the loop over self.processes breaks when the deadline is exceeded (`if remaining_time <= 0: break`). Because `process.terminate()` is only executed after the per-process wait loop, any processes not yet iterated will never reach the terminate call and can remain alive. The previous single-process implementation always executed `terminate()` after the wait. This is a real behavioral regression visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SpanFlusher.join() gives self.next_step.join(timeout) the full timeout up front instead of the remaining time, so if next_step consumes it, remaining_time <= 0 is true on the first iteration and zero processes are terminated

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), a single `deadline` is computed before calling `self.next_step.join(timeout)`, but the full `timeout` is passed to `next_step` rather than the remaining time. If `next_step.join(timeout)` consumes (most/all of) the timeout, then `remaining_time = deadline - time.time()` will be `<= 0` on the first process iteration, triggering `break` and skipping the subsequent `process.terminate()` calls for all processes. This can leave flusher processes running after join() returns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _ensure_processes_alive: process.kill() is guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), so in thread mode (produce_to_pipe set) a hang restart starts a new thread for the same shards while the old hung thread keeps running — if the old thread recovers, both poll the same shards and call produce_to_pipe, causing duplicate segment production; this replaces the old loud Thread.kill() AttributeError with a new silent failure mode

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, unhealthy thread-mode workers (created when `produce_to_pipe` is set, i.e. `make_process = threading.Thread`) are “restarted” by calling `_create_process_for_shards(...)` without any mechanism to stop/kill the old thread. The code explicitly only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` (so threads are never stopped), and it also does not set `self.stopped` during restarts. This can leave the old thread running while a new thread for the same `shards` is started, meaning both can concurrently poll/flush the same shards and invoke `produce_to_pipe`, creating a real risk of duplicate production and a leaked/hanging thread. This is a new silent failure mode compared to the previous behavior where attempting `.kill()` on a thread would raise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric tag inconsistency in flusher.py main(): spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes use tags={'shard': shard_tag} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses tags={'shards': shard_tag}, so existing dashboards/alerts keyed on one tag name won't see the other timer

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main()` the diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys for shard identification: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`. This inconsistency is real and diff-grounded and can disrupt existing dashboards/alerts or aggregations expecting a single tag name, but it’s an observability/schema issue rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: shard_tag is a comma-joined list of all shards in the process (e.g. '0,1,2,...,63'), so timer tag cardinality scales with the number of distinct shard-subsets across consumers rather than with shard count; the timers should match the sane per-shard form used by the flusher_unhealthy counter

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.main, the code builds `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` and uses it in metrics tags for timers (e.g. `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`). Since `shards` is the full list assigned to that process (potentially multiple shards), the tag value becomes a shard-subset string (e.g. "0,2"), which can increase metric tag cardinality based on shard-groupings. This differs from `_ensure_processes_alive`, which reports `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` per shard using `tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard}`. The finding is a concrete, diff-grounded observability concern (cardinality/consistency), not a functional correctness defect.
